brief.objective: Drive trial signups for Guidde by making a UGC-style story ad that earns attention through narrative before revealing the product, positioned for paid social (Meta/TikTok feed).
brief.audience: Individual contributors and team leads in ops, IT, support, and cross-functional roles who are the informal 'go-to' person for how things work — overworked, under-recognized, tired of repeating themselves.
brief.winning_formula: The 'earned reveal' testimonial formula: 8 of 10 shots are pure story with zero product, the product appears in exactly 2 adjacent shots at the runtime's midpoint, those 2 shots are cut noticeably faster than everything around them, and the ad closes on a status claim instead of a benefit claim. It works because it disguises an ad as a personal confession long enough that the audience's guard is down when the product appears, and it makes the payoff about the viewer's standing at work, not the software's feature set — which is far more shareable and far less skippable.
brief.adaptation_rationale: Carried over: single handheld presenter talking direct-to-camera, a contrarian imperative hook, a mid-ad two-shot demo (capture, then artifact) placed dead-centre, an accelerating edit into the demo, and a status/leverage payoff. Changed: the scenario moves from 'surviving a micromanaging boss' to 'being the single point of knowledge-failure on a team' — a broader, less HR-risky pain that still produces the same posture (undismissable). The product beat is now explicitly Guidde (capture once, auto-generated walkthrough) instead of a competitor's UI. The payoff line is rewritten as a career-visibility claim, not a firing-avoidance claim. The weak spoken-only CTA is upgraded to a clean end card with headline, button, and URL — the one deliberate structural improvement.
brief.hook: If you're the only person who knows how something works, don't just quietly panic every time you go on vacation.
brief.angle: Becoming the person leadership can't overlook — not by working more, but by making your knowledge visible without extra effort, using Guidde to auto-document your process as you do it.
brief.key_message: You don't have to choose between doing the work and getting credit for knowing it — Guidde turns the work you already do into proof, automatically.
brief.tone_and_casting: One presenter, mid-30s, casual and slightly wry, talking straight into a phone camera, handheld, in a lived-in home office. Conspiratorial register — talking to a peer who's also tired of being everyone's tribal knowledge, not pitching them.
brief.format_specs: 9:16 vertical, ~43 seconds, phone-shot handheld UGC look, natural available light, no music bed, continuous fragment captions (2-4 words) burned in bold white sans-serif with black outline, centered, synced to speech; final 3 seconds cut to a static end card.
brief.cta: End card: Guidde logo, headline 'Turn what you know into proof,' button 'Try Guidde Free,' URL guidde.com supered cleanly — no clutter, 3-second hold.
